title: deinit and Object Lifetime
hints: `deinit` runs the moment the last strong reference to an object disappears.
Removing the first element releases it immediately; the rest are released when the array's `do { }` scope ends.
jsBridge: `deinit` runs **deterministically** when the last strong reference goes away (ARC). JS garbage collection is non-deterministic, and `FinalizationRegistry` callbacks may never run. In Swift you can rely on `deinit` for cleanup such as removing observers.

compass.q: JS has no destructors you can rely on. What cleanup patterns (dispose, AbortController) become simpler with deterministic `deinit`?
Java's `finalize` was deprecated for being unpredictable. Why is Swift's `deinit` predictable?
When exactly does a local variable's object deinit: end of scope or last use? (Swift can release early after last use.)
Printing in `deinit` is the classic way to detect view controller leaks. How would you automate it in tests?
